name: Kepler-13
description: Star of 7,650 K, 519 parsecs away, with 1 transiting planet.

radius.source: Esteves et al. 2015, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of KOI-13 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive

mass.source: Esteves et al. 2015, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of KOI-13 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive

temperature.source: Esteves et al. 2015, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of KOI-13 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive

color.reason: Kepler-13 B lies 1.2 arcsec away and gives 47% of the light (WDS 19079+4652, Mason et al. 2001): every spectrum and catalogue color of the star blends the two, so the color is taken from its own temperature

text.card: Kepler-13 b crosses Kepler-13 as seen from Earth, which is how it was found.
text.introduction: Its radius and temperature follow Esteves et al. 2015.
text.locator: NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (st_refname ESTEVES_ET_AL__2015): st_teff 7650, st_rad 1.74, st_mass 1.72

quotes.title: Kepler-13
quotes.card: Kepler-13 or KOI-13 is a triple star system consisting of Kepler-13A, around which an orbiting hot Jupiter exoplanet was discovered with the Kepler space telescope in 2011, and Kepler-13B a common proper motion companion star which has an additional star orbiting it.

radialVelocity.source: No catalogued radial velocity: Gaia DR3 measures none for source 2130632159136095104 and SIMBAD lists none. Zero is assumed; a 30 km/s error moves the star by one part in 200,000 of its distance per century
